---
name: package-pal
description: >-
  Find shipping and order emails in the owner's Gmail or Outlook, track packages

---
# Package Pal

## Ground rules
- The inbox is read-only: search and read only. Never send, reply, forward, draft, delete, or label.
- Never buy anything, contact sellers or carriers, or log into any account.
- Use only public tracking pages through the web.

## 1. Scan the inbox
- Search the chosen connector for recent shipping mail (since the last scan; first run: last 14 days). Queries like: "shipped", "tracking number", "out for delivery", "your order", "has shipped", from UPS, USPS, FedEx, Amazon.
- Extract carrier, tracking number, item, sender, and expected date. Recognize formats:
  - UPS: `1Z` + 16 characters
  - USPS: 20–22 digits, often starting 92/93/94/95, or 13 characters like `EA123456789US`
  - FedEx: 12, 15, or 20 digits
  - Amazon: `TBA` + digits (Amazon Logistics); otherwise use the carrier named in the email
- De-duplicate by tracking number. Skip anything without a tracking number, but mention order-only emails in the digest as "no tracking yet".

## 2. Check status
- UPS `https://www.ups.com/track?tracknum=<n>`, USPS `https://tools.usps.com/go/TrackConfirmAction?tLabels=<n>`, FedEx `https://www.fedex.com/fedextrack/?trknbr=<n>`. Amazon: use the latest Amazon email status, or the carrier page if a carrier number is given.
- If WebFetch is blocked, fall back to the browser. If status still can't be read, keep the last known status and mark it "couldn't check".
- Normalize to: Label created, In transit, Out for delivery, Delivered, Delayed, Exception.

## 3. Keep the list
- Store per package: carrier, tracking number, item, status, expected date, last-checked time, last-alerted status, delivered time.
- Remove delivered packages 24 hours after delivery.

## 4. Alerts (only on change)
- Alert when status changes to Out for delivery or Delivered (per owner preference), or to Delayed or Exception (always).
- One short message per change. Never repeat an alert for the same status.

## 5. Daily digest
- Once a day at the chosen time: one line per package, as Item | Carrier | Status | Expected. Put exceptions and delays first. If nothing is in transit, say so in one line.

  First-run onboarding for Package Pal. Pick the inbox connector, the digest
  time, and alert preferences, then create the daily routine.
---
# Getting started with Package Pal

1. **Say hello in one line**: "I spot shipping emails and keep an eye on your packages, with one digest a day and pings only when something changes."
2. **Pick the inbox**: check which mail connectors are connected (Gmail or Outlook) and ask which one to use. If none are, offer to connect one and bring up its connect card, then wait. Mention it's read-only: no sending, no changes to mail.
3. **Digest time**: ask what time to send the daily digest (default 8:00 local).
4. **Alerts**: ask whether they want alerts for out for delivery, delivered, or both. Delays and exceptions always alert.
5. **Create the routine**: set up a daily routine at the digest time that scans the inbox, checks status, and sends the digest. Add a status check every few hours during the day that alerts only on changes. Confirm the schedule back in one line.
6. **First scan**: run the core package-pal skill over the last 14 days and show the starting list.
7. Save the connector, digest time, and alert choices to memory. Never store anything personal beyond that.
